text:
alex: :rotating_light: Runtime alerts — continuous-batcher queue in us-west-1 is growing unbounded, pods hitting OOM and node flaps. Seeing repeated CUDA OOMs on batch-worker-3 and eviction churn. Impacting inference latencies and 5xxs for some customers.

incident-bot: Alert triggered: continuous-batcher.queue_depth > 10000 (us-west-1). Escalation policy: eng-oncall -> 15m.

mira: grabbing this. which pool is hit? dedicated-gpu-pool-2?

alex: yes, dedicated-gpu-pool-2. metrics: queue depth 12k, p99 latency spiked from 120ms -> 3.2s, error rate to Redwood API for route /v1/generate up to 8%. AcmeCorp reported 504s.

jen-sre: logs show batch accumulation loop not draining due to a deadlock in continuous-batcher inflight accounting. stack trace excerpt:```
E Batcher: enqueue() waiting on condvar for 120s
E Batcher: KVCache prefetch in progress, cannot evict
E runtime: cuda: out of memory (allocated=7.9GiB)
```

ops-luis: node pov — node gpu-12 had oom-kill for nvidia-container-runtime, kubelet restarted container, node marked NotReady briefly. We saw kube-proxy churn on the host during restart.

mira: immediate mitigation plan: 1) set continuous-batcher.max_queue_depth=1000 (soft cap + drop oldest) 2) toggle prefetch_enabled=false for the batch shard to reduce KV cache growth 3) drain one problematic node and cordon the rest for safe restarts 4) scale up pool by +2 GPUs as short-term buffer.

alex: commands I ran:```bash
# soft cap config patch
curl -X PATCH -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \n  https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/configs/continuous-batcher \n  -d '{"max_queue_depth":1000, "drop_policy":"oldest"}'
# disable prefetch for shard-7
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \n  https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/shards/7/actions -d '{"action":"set_prefetch","value":false}'
```

mira: applied the config change and toggled prefetch. queue depth fell from 12k -> 2.1k over 4m. p99 down to ~700ms but still above normal. nodes still flapping; I'm draining gpu-12 and restarting docker runtime there.

support-emily: Customer comms: AcmeCorp gateways showed ~30% increased timeouts starting 09:14 UTC, we sent a proactive note and asked for logs. They confirmed some requests got 504s and retried. Internal SLOs affected for the checkout flow.

jen-sre: follow-up diag: looks like the deadlock happens when prefetch + long-running batched requests increase cumulative KV cache and we hit host memory limits -> swap/paging leading to severe latency. Essentially a paging cascade. Disabling prefetch prevents new KV growth while we drain.

ops-luis: I restarted container on gpu-12, cleared the CUDA context. Node rejoined. Kept cordon on gpu-13 which had intermittent SIGKILLs.

mira: additional mitigations: - enabled batcher backpressure circuit: when queue_depth>2000 we now reject small/cheap routes (reroute to fallback smaller model) - enabled auto-fallback policy for model_variant->quantized-v1 for non-critical customers.

alex: metrics update: 10m after mitigations, error rate down to 1.2%, p99 ~320ms, queue depth ~400. Still monitoring for recurrence. :eyes: 

incident-bot: Incident annotated: runbook "continuous-batcher/paging-cascade" applied (mitigations: cap, prefetch disable, node drain, fallback).

mira: I'm going to keep watch for one hour and then hand off to next oncall. Please keep an eye on these dashboards: /dashboards/continuous-batcher/us-west1, /dashboards/kvcache/evictions.

jen-sre: please file an incident postmortem and include root cause hypothesis: combination of prefetch-induced KV growth + lack of queue caps + eviction path regression from last runtime release. Possible fixes: proper backpressure in enqueue path, safer prefetch budget, enforce host memory guardrails.

support-emily: Logged customer impact ticket ACME-4523 with timeline and what we did. Will include suggested mitigations for retries on their side.

alex: notes for follow-up action items: - revert risky prefetch changes in next deploy candidate - add e2e sim to stress test prefetch + batching at scale - add hard host memory guard and kill-signal telemetry to catch OOM before node flaps - run chaos test to ensure node restarts don't cause cascade.

mira: handing off to jen-sre for PM and postmortem work. I'll update the incident channel if anything regrows. :shipit: 

jen-sre: ack, picking up postmortem. saving logs to /incidents/4975001234 and scheduling RCA meeting.

alex: thanks all.
